{"rule": "Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and a new passage of about 250 words in the text field.", "text": "The woman at the counter did not ask for his name. She asked for his number, and when Tomas said he did not have one, she looked at him for the first time, as though a number were the thing that made a person visible.

"Everyone has a number," she said.

"I was told I had two."

She did not smile. She typed something, and the screen in front of her threw a pale light up onto her chin. Behind him the queue shifted, a collective sigh of coats and shopping bags. Someone's child was counting the floor tiles aloud and getting it wrong each time in a different way.

"Date of birth," she said.

He gave it. She typed again, then stopped, and her hands stayed above the keys the way hands do when they have found something they were not looking for.

"There are two entries," she said.

"Yes."

"They don't agree."

"No."

She looked at him properly now, and Tomas saw her decide that he was not the kind of problem she was paid to solve. He had seen the look before, on the man with the folder, on the clerk at the post office, on a doctor who had asked him twice where he had grown up and written down neither answer.

"You'll need to go upstairs," she said.

"Which room?"

She hesitated, and in the hesitation he heard his mother laughing, somewhere far off, delighted as always by a question with more than one answer.

"It depends," the woman said, "which one of you is asking.""}
